statements.text: There are $9000$ four-digit counting numbers, from $1000$ to $9999$.
There are $9999$ four-digit counting numbers, counting every whole number from $1$ through $9999$.
A $4$-digit number has digit length $4$, so there are exactly $4$ such numbers.

stem:
Rohan asks how many $4$-digit counting numbers there are.

Which statements are correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Four-digit counting numbers run from 1000 to 9999, so there are 9000 of them. Statement 1 alone is correct. Statement 2 counts from 1 and drops the 4-digit start. Statement 3 confuses digit length with the count of such numbers.
